sentences.text: Brief facts as per the prosecution case are that the petitioners in connivance with co-accused have duped the complainant for a sum of 12,50,000/- by refusing to get the sale CRM-M-5921-2026 deed executed and also denied to return the earnest money.
Hence, the present FIR.
Learned counsel for the petitioners argues that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further submits that the complainant is himself a Punjab Police official and by using his influence, he got the present FIR registered based upon false allegations.
He submits that the present FIR was lodged after a delay of 7 months casting serious doubt upon the prosecution story.
He further submits that no amount has been received by the petitioners, hence, nothing is to be recovered from them.

He further submits that the petitioners were directed to join the investigation by the Id. trial Court, but, the said order was vacated as the prosecution took a stand that the amount involved is yet to be recovered.
Learned counsel has further submitted that the petitioners are ready and willing to join the investigation as and when called upon to do so by the investigating agency.
He submits that the present dispute is purely civil in nature which has been given criminal color by the complainant to harass the petitioners.

In support of his arguments, learned counsel has placed reliance in the case of 'Sharif Ahmed and another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another' 2024 INSC 363, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:
"... Any effort to settle civil disputes and claims which do not involve any criminal offence, by applying pressure through criminal prosecution should be deprecated and discouraged".

"Prima facie, in our opinion, breach of contract does not amount to an offence under Section 420 or Section 406 of the IPC unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is S026: PRG 0927S:
CRM-M-5921-2026 me Shown right at the beginning of the transaction.

sentences.text: This Court has time and again cautioned against converting purely civil disputes into criminal cases.
Any effort to settle civil disputes and claims, which do not involve any criminal offence, by applying pressure through criminal prosecution should be deprecated and discouraged."
Notice of motion.
On asking of the Court, Mr. Ravinder Singh, DAG, Punjab, accepts notice on behalf of respondent No.1-State and seeks time to file status report in the matter.

sentences.text: At this stage, Mr. Deepanshu Mehta, Advocate has put in appearance on behalf of complainant and filed his Vakalatnama, which is taken on record.
He, while opposing the petition for anticipatory bail, has contended that the petitioner has cheated the complainant to the tune of 12,50,000/-.

He further argued that the present petitioner never intended to execute the sale deed whereas the complainant was always ready and willing to perform his part of the agreement and now he has even retised to return the earnest money.
Adjourned to 10.02.2026.

In the meantime, the petitioners are directed to join investigation within a week from today and would appear as and when required by the Investigating Officer and cooperate with the Investigating Agency.
In the event of arrest, they shall be admitted to interim bail on furnishing of bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of Arresting/Investigating Officer.
The petitioners shall also abide by the conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) of BNSS, 2023."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that in compliance of the order dated 02.02.2026 passed by this Court, the petitioners have joined the investigation.
Learned counsel for the State, on instructions from ASI Rakesh Kumar, has submitted that the petitioners have joined the investigation and is no longer required for further investigation.
5. Learned counsel for the complainant appears and submits that the offence committed by the petitioners is serious in nature and they do not deserve concession of bail.
6. In view of the statement made by learned State counsel, the interim order dated 02.02.2026 is made absolute.
The petitioners shall continue to join investigation, as and when called by the Investigating Officer and shall also abide by the conditions as provided under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
(RUPINDERJIT CHAHAL) 27.02.2026 JUDGE Mohit Bishnoi i) Whether speaking/reasoned? Yes/No ii) Whether reportable?
